title: Bounded-above complexes resolved by a zero-preserving left resolution
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category] with a zero object and finite coproducts, and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful and additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Suppose $Q:A\to C$ is a functor preserving zero morphisms and $\pi:\iota Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ is a natural transformation with epimorphic components. On the full subcategory of integer cochain complexes whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees, there are a functor $S$ to integer cochain complexes in $A$ and a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota_-$, where $\iota_-$ is the inclusion, such that every $a_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $S(L)$ is isomorphic to an object in the essential image of $\iota$, and every upper bound for $L$ is an upper bound for $S(L)$. This functor is defined on all maps in the bounded-above full subcategory, regardless of which upper-bound witnesses are chosen.

proof.text: Package Q, π, and hπ as Λ : CategoryTheory.Abelian.LeftResolution ι. Its functor is definitionally Q, so it preserves zero morphisms.

Use the existing proved source construction Λ.minusResolutionFunctor : Minus A ⥤ Minus C, followed by ι.mapCochainComplexMinus and Minus.ι A, for S. This is the total of the objectwise resolution, mapped termwise by ι. Whisker the existing Λ.minusResolutionNatTrans with Minus.ι A to obtain a : S ⟶ Minus.ι A. The source instance QuasiIso ((Functor.whiskerRight Λ.minusResolutionNatTrans (Minus.ι A)).app L) supplies the component quasi-isomorphisms. The existing source implementation already combines the objectwise cochain resolution [lem-sfb-left-resolution-objectwise-cochain], the bounded-column comparison [lem-pc-bounded-above-double-complex-total-comparison], total transport via mapTotalIso, and the single-row identification [lem-sfb-left-resolution-single-row-total]; no separate statement-only wrapper is needed.

proof.text: For L and i, take X to be the i-th term of (Λ.minusResolutionFunctor.obj L).obj. The term (S.obj L).X i is definitionally ι.obj X, so Iso.refl provides the essential-image isomorphism.

Given any b and hL : L.obj.IsStrictlyLE b, install hL as a local instance. The source total-support instance gives IsStrictlyLE ((Λ.bicomplexFunctor.obj L.obj).total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) b; termwise mapping by ι preserves strict support. This proves the upper-bound clause for every b without altering the functor or choosing bound-dependent maps.
